mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 4% in the month prior to the prediction is associated with a short-term negative pressure on equity discount rates, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4% in the prior month
regime_hint: tightening phase of the Fed Funds rate
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive or flat despite FEDFUNDS > 4% for ≥2 consecutive months prior.

mechanism_narrative: Rising monthly employment (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) suggests a labor market strengthening without cost-push pressures, predicting positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while CPIAUCSL decreases over the prior month
regime_hint: labor market strengthening without inflationary pressures
failure_condition: 60-day returns are negative or flat despite the described labor-inflation pattern persists.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 2% for two consecutive months is interpreted as a growing goods-demand signal, forecasting positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative despite INDPRO growth >2% for ≥2 months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in the RSAFS (residential starts) accompanied by a decline in the GDPC1 (personal consumption) suggests supply-side weakness, predicting negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS falls by >10% while GDPC1 falls by >3% in the prior month
regime_hint: supply-side contraction in housing and consumption
failure_condition: 5-day returns are positive or flat despite the specified contraction pattern.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains below 2% for three consecutive months in a non-recessionary regime, it signals accommodative policy, associated with positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) over the 3-month FEDFUNDS < 2% window.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in unemployment benefits claims (PAYEMS) followed by a subsequent rise in UNRATE indicates labor market adjustment, predicting negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >15% in a month while UNRATE rises in the following month
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive despite the described labor adjustment pattern.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the monthly CPIAUCSL (inflation) below 2% for two consecutive months in a stable macro environment is interpreted as deflationary pressure, forecasting positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 60-day returns are negative despite CPIAUCSL < 2% for ≥2 months.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising consumer spending (GDPC1) without a corresponding rise in housing starts (RSAFS) suggests demand-driven growth, predicting positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increases while RSAFS remains flat or declines over the prior two months
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not significantly positive (rank IC > 0.05) during the pattern.
